title: The Dragon's Roost
enemy_health_note:
What a kind of enemy is worth ON THIS LEVEL, overriding the health in its profile (features/combat/enemy.gd). Applied at spawn by _build_world in game/session.gd.

The dragon is two different fights and only one of them is this one. On The Fractured Isles it is the whole boss and 1275 - twenty-one clean hits of the jumped kick at 60 - is the size of that fight. Here it shares the deck with a Dragon Lord who is 1275 himself, and two of those back to back is a last level that is longer than the one before it rather than harder. 969 is sixteen kicks, twenty-one blasts or forty-eight punches, and it keeps both of the dragon's phases - eleven seconds up, six down - running more than once, which is what went wrong the last time this number was cut (it was 240 on the isles, four kicks, and the fight ended before either phase had played).

EVERY ONE OF THESE NUMBERS CAME DOWN 15% together: the dragon's profile 1500 to 1275, the Lord's 1500 to 1275, and this override 1140 to 969. The fights were long rather than hard, and the ratio between the wall and the harasser is what was tuned, so taking the same percentage off all three keeps that shape and only shortens them. Sixteen kicks still runs the dragon's up-and-down cycle more than once, which is the floor this number has.

The Lord is not listed here because no other level places him, so his 1275 lives in his profile where anyone reading the cast can see it. tests/diag_boss_health.gd prints every boss on every level with the clean-hit count for each of the player's attacks, and is the before-and-after for any change to either number.
boss_music_note:
The battle loop that takes over the moment the fight starts and holds until both bosses are beaten, then hands back to the level's own magic_cliffs loop for the aftermath. The same track The Fractured Isles' dragon fights to - xDeviruchi's Decisive Battle - because this is the same coast's last stand and there is one battle theme on it. The Dragon Lord is the last boss in the game and he fights to the game's battle theme; a stand-in was tried here and taken back out.

THE FILE HAS TO BE PUT BACK for either level to actually play it. decisive_battle.wav is not in the repository: `*.wav` is gitignored with no exception for godot/audio/ the way there is one for the mp3s, and Assests/ is outside the clone, so scripts/extract_boss_music.py cannot regenerate it on a fresh machine. Until it is there music.gd finds nothing, warns, and leaves the coast loop running under BOTH dragon fights - this level's and the isles'. The fix is one command and no code change, because .ogg is deliberately not gitignored: ffmpeg -i "Assests/xDeviruchi - Decisive Battle.wav" -q:a 5 godot/audio/decisive_battle.ogg. See PROVENANCE.md in godot/audio/. session.gd asks current_track() every tick (see it, and boss_fighting() ), so dying back to the spawn brings the quiet loop back with the player rather than leaving him to walk to battle music, and the walk-in cutscene keeps it ducked until the dialogue is done - the fight track comes in as the picture hands the level back, not under it.

BOTH is the operative word, and it was not always true. current_track() used to ask boss(), which is the FIRST boss that is engaged and on screen, and this level lists the dragon first: beating the dragon handed the coast loop back under a Dragon Lord who was still swinging, and took it away again four and a half seconds later when the dragon's body finally left the level. boss_fighting() asks for any boss still on its feet instead, so either order of deaths holds the track - see tests/diag_boss_track.gd, which walks both levels through both orders, and tests/diag_battle_music.gd, which reads the same beats off a real audio driver.
brief: One ledge, one dragon, and nowhere on it he cannot reach you.
scope: The last level on the course, and the whole of it is the final boss fight. There is no platforming here worth the name - a hop in, an arena, a flag - because the level IS the fight and anything else would be in the way of it.
fight_note:
The dragon fights in two phases and the arena has to hold both.

IN THE AIR it is the only thing in the game with no feet on the ground, and three numbers follow from that. See the "dragon" profile and the flying block in features/combat/enemy.gd.

  * It cruises 156 above the deck it took off from. A player on the flat reaches 143 at the top of a jump, so from the floor it cannot be hit at all. Standing there waiting is legitimate and slow.
  * The two floating stones are 96 up. A jump from one reaches 239, well into it. That is the only reason they exist, and why there are two at opposite ends of the arena: the dragon circles, and a single perch you can be cornered on is a trap rather than an answer.
  * It answers a thrown blast by climbing over it, unless the throw was inside its reaction - 168 px cold, 76 once it has seen one and is braced for the next. So the energy strike still beats it, at knife range, and only while it is down. Which is the same lesson the guard taught on the way here, asked again by something that cannot block.

ON ITS FEET it is an ordinary bruiser and the arena needs nothing special for it: it walks in at 150, which is outrunnable like everything else in the cast, claws at 86 and breathes the standing version of the same fire from 125 to 180. Nine seconds up, seven down, with a drawn take-off and landing between them that cannot be interrupted. That phase is why the deck is as long as it is - there has to be somewhere to back off to - and the gap at 720 is the one thing in the level it will not follow you over.

The deck is dead flat on purpose. A flyer measures every altitude it holds from the height it took off at, so a perch standing above or below the ground the fight happens over would put its whole envelope in the wrong place.
ground_note: The same numbers The Fractured Isles and First Steps are cut with, so all three levels are visibly the same coast. features/world/scenery.gd generates every cliff from `solids`, so the art cannot drift off the collision.
solids_note:
The approach ends at 720 and the arena starts at 816 - a 96 px hop, 45% of the jump envelope, and the gentlest crossing on the course. It is there to say the level has started, not to test anything. The two floating stones are the pack's own islands, 96 above the deck against a 107 apex, and they are the only thing in the arena that is not flat.

The arena is three touching blocks of different depths rather than one, which is the only thing this level's geometry does differently. features/world/scenery.gd draws rock edges at the ENDS of a solid, and a boss arena is by nature one long unbroken deck with both ends off screen - as a single 2064-wide block it came out as a flat black band under a grass line, with none of the broken rock the rest of the coast is made of. Three blocks put a torn rock column at each seam, and stopping them 168 to 240 down instead of 1452 puts open sea under the island. Nothing about the surface changes: all three top out at 648, the turf runs over the joins, and from up there it is one rock.
boss_arena_note:
The x the fight is sealed behind, and the west edge of the room all three of them are shut into - the player by a wall built in _build_arena (game/session.gd), the dragon by fly_bounds. Same rule as The Fractured Isles: a boss is the one thing you may not walk away from, because both bosses are bounded to their arena and a player who left it stood somewhere neither could follow.

816 is the lip of the middle deck, the first ground east of the only gap in this level (720..816). It is NOT 1512, the lip of the deck the two of them actually stand on: the west floating stone is at 1188, and a wall at 1512 would shut one of the two perches - the only way to reach the flying dragon - out of its own fight. It is not 720 either, the far lip of the gap, because a wall there is one you hit in mid-air over a fall.

The cutscene cues at 900, 84 past the line, so the fight is sealed from the moment the panels hand the level back. The flag at 2544 is past the gate at 2400 and therefore outside the arena, so this can never shut him in with the level finished.

WHAT IT COSTS: the milk bottle at 540 and the brew at 624 are on the spawn deck, west of the line, so neither is reachable once the fight is on. Two bosses and no top-up inside the room. Drinking before you cross the gap is the intended reading - the two crates at 900 and 966 are inside, so there are throwables - but if that is too thin, move one bottle east of 816 rather than moving the wall.
gates_note:
One gate, and the dragon holds it. It perches at 2100, inside the section, so the wall at 2400 stays shut until it is beaten and its body is gone - a boss holds its section through its whole death, which on this level keeps the camera on the arena while it collapses and climbs out - and while it is shut the camera stops with the wall on the right edge of the screen, which is what frames the arena. Nothing blocks going back: retreating over the hop is a real answer to a swoop.

The wall is the dragon's limit too, not just the player's. session.gd fences a flyer into the section it was placed in - see fly_bounds in features/combat/enemy.gd - because a flyer has no floor to run out from under it and backs away from a player who crowds it, so one cornered against a shut gate would otherwise be pushed out through the side of the screen. tests/diag_arena.gd is the measurement: 272 frames of 900 off screen before the fence, none after.
hazards_note: None, for the reason The Fractured Isles gives: spikes kill outright whatever your health is, and this is a health-bar fight from the moment the gate shuts. The sea under the hop is the only thing here that can finish you without the dragon doing it.
enemies_note: Two bosses, side by side, and the gate at 2400 waits on BOTH. They stand a body apart at the centre of the deck — the Dragon Lord at 1620 and the dragon at 1800 — so the fight opens with the pair of them together and the dragon takes off out of the middle of it. The Lord is the bipedal bruiser that held the Isles archway before the dragon took that fight (see the dragon_lord profile in features/combat/enemy.gd): he wakes inside his 460 of aggro and walks in at 52, and on The Dragon's Roost he is turned up to a boss — he is unflinching (no blow of yours staggers or turns him, only footwork beats him), his hits fling you off your feet, and his close-range special is a leap-slam whose landing shocks the ground around where he comes down. The dragon takes off inside its 560 and breathes far more often here than it did alone (special_cooldown 2.5), to keep the air thick with fire over the Lord. Both stand on the deck like any other enemy, so scripts/check_levels.py can measure them, and both hold the gate, so the wall stays shut until the arena is cleared. The two floating stones are still the only way to reach the dragon in the air, and neither the Lord's claw nor his slam-shock can reach a player up on them — 108 px above him, clear of the 96 the shock rises — so they stay the safe perch they were. On the HUD the Lord holds the plate's main green bar and the dragon the red one beneath it: two bosses, two meters. See boss_main/boss_second in game/session.gd and the boss block in ui/hud.gd. He is the longer of the two fights as well as the closer one: 1275 against the dragon's 969 here (see enemy_health above), so he is the wall and the thing overhead is the harassment.
crates_note: Two, at the mouth of the arena. Nobody needs targets to learn on this late - these are cover you can pick up and throw, and the last thing in the level a blast will reliably connect with.
bottles_note: Milk and brew, three bars of five each, stood side by side on the approach rather than inside the arena. Everything the fight needs is picked up before the fight: once the gate shuts there is no topping up.
signs_note: Deliberately none. The two it used to carry - the 07 / THE ROOST title and the IT SEES YOU warning - are gone: by the final level there is nothing left to introduce, and the two-panel cutscene as you walk in says everything the signs did and more. Nothing on this level is a hint any more; the fight speaks for itself.
decor_note: [x, y, piece] with the piece's bottom edge at y; a fourth value tilts it. The two rock_mass entries hang from the sky, and both are deliberately OUTSIDE the arena - one over the approach, one over the flag. A hanging mass over the fight would sit in exactly the air the dragon cruises in (492 world), and the boss would spend the whole fight drawn in front of a rock. Art only, never collision.

cutscene.caption: Lugia! Who did this to you? Who's dared to hurt the scales of the ancient blood?
YOU! pathetic human, this island warden. I will shatter your bones just as I have shattered many such pitiful worlds.
You claim this rock, Warden. For now! I will be back with vengeance!
...and I will be waiting right here at my fragmented islands, demon!
THANK YOU FOR PLAYING
cutscene.end_credit: music by Marllon Silva (a.k.a) xDeviruchi  ·  art by Ansimuz

boss_departs_note:
The beaten dragon stays where it falls on this level instead of getting up and flying out. Applied at spawn by _build_world in game/session.gd; see `departs` and _advance_flyer_death in features/combat/enemy.gd.

The flight out is THE FRACTURED ISLES' ENDING, not something dragons do. That level's second story card is a picture of the dragon leaving, and the body climbing out of the shot behind the picture is the whole point of it - the card is cued between the fall and the departure precisely so the two line up. This level ends on the Dragon Lord and the Warden instead, and a dragon flapping away over that exchange is a second thing happening during the last beat of the game, pulling the eye off the two characters actually speaking.

So here it collapses, lies on the deck through the victory cards, and is cleared after the same DEAD_LINGER every other body gets. Nothing else changes: it still has to come down on a solid rather than over the gap (see the glide in _advance_flyer_death), because a body that falls out of the world still takes the ending with it.
finish_after_cutscene_note:
The level ends on its last story card instead of on its flag. See _finish_if_the_cards_were_the_ending in game/session.gd.

The whole of this level is the boss fight. Once both bosses are down and the three victory cards have played, the flag is 700 px of empty arena the player has already walked, with nothing in it and nothing to decide - the cards are the ending and the walk is a lap of honour nobody asked for. So the last card hands straight to the completion screen, and from there the course is over and the title comes back (see State.COMPLETE in session.gd).

The flag is still built and still solid. Nothing about reaching it changed; this only means you no longer have to.
cutscene_note:
Two panels as he walks in, the same machinery The Fractured Isles uses (see cutscene_note there and _advance_story in game/session.gd). `panel` names a file in ui/art/storyboard and `audio` a file in audio/, both without extension, all written by scripts/extract_storyboard.py from the raw art in Assests/Storyboard. Both are 16:9 already (~1.79) rather than the isles cards' 4:3, so the extractor trims their width instead of their height.

THE SEQUENCE plays at x 900 - 84 px past the arena mouth at 816 and short of either boss's aggro (the Lord's 460 reaches to 1160, the dragon's 560 to 1240), so the picture is what starts the fight rather than the walk into it, exactly as on the isles. Both cards carry the same `at`, so the second follows the first: dragon_lord_fight_start is the Lord kneeling with the drake, then dragon_lord_fight_start_2 is the pair of them turning on you.

ONE CLIP, SPREAD ACROSS BOTH. dragon_lord_fight is 21.3 s of dialogue with its content ending at 18 and pauses at about 7 s and 11.6 s. If the first panel simply held for the whole clip the second would not arrive until 21 s in - which is what it did. So the clip is pinned across the two panels instead: the first panel holds an explicit 5.8 s and the second keeps the SAME clip running ("keep_audio": true) rather than restarting it, so the cut from panel one to panel two lands on the ~7 s pause, on the dialogue's own beat, and the second panel carries the rest of it. `keep_audio` and an explicit `hold` are the two fields that make that work - see _read_story_card, _begin_story and _begin_story_out in session.gd. Move the 5.8 to move where the second panel comes in.

ON THE WAY OUT the cutscene wakes BOTH bosses together - see _wake_boss in session.gd, which was one-boss until this level and now engages every boss the card hands the level to. Both cards can be skipped ("skip": true), like the isles' and like every card in the game; they play once per visit, not per attempt, so a retry drops you straight back into the fight without one either way.

WHAT THEY SAY is printed under the picture as a subtitle: `caption` on each card, laid out bottom-centred on the same scrim the opening's captions use - see _set_story_line in session.gd. Both panels carry one, because both are spoken over; the isles' second card has none because it is a picture of the dragon leaving with nobody left to talk over it. The lines follow the clip's own two halves, which is why the split is where it is. tests/diag_speech.gd puts five runs of sound in the clip - 0.48-2.96 and 3.42-6.70 are the first line's two sentences, then 7.40-8.22 (the shout, and the loudest thing in the clip), 8.46-11.44 and 12.12-18.10 are the second's three - and tests/capture_roost_cutscene.gd measures the line changing hands at 7.01 s, in the 0.70 s gap between them: 0.31 after the first finishes and 0.39 before the second starts. Moving the 5.8 moves the subtitle along with the picture, so it has to stay in that gap. The delivery direction that came with the script - the first line is angry - is not printed; it is in the voice.

THE THREE CARDS AFTER THE FIGHT are cued off `after: "bosses_down"`, not `boss_down`. This level is the only one that fights two bosses, and `boss_down` fires on the FIRST of them to drop - which would stop the world for a victory card while the survivor was still hitting a player who cannot move. `bosses_down` waits for all of them; see _bosses_all_fallen in session.gd, which is a second function rather than a flag on the first so that the isles' cue cannot change behaviour because this level needed a stricter one.

THE SPLIT BETWEEN THEM is measured, not guessed, but it is NOT verified against the words. dragon_lord_defeated.mp3 is 13.479 s and tests/diag_speech.gd finds seven runs of sound in it: 0.24-2.42, 2.62-3.50, 4.16-6.48, then a 0.80 s gap, 7.28-7.64, then 8.46-10.18, 10.60-12.20 and 12.82-13.54. The two biggest gaps are 0.80 before 7.28 and 0.82 before 8.46, which are too close to separate on energy alone. The cut is placed at 6.9, inside the first of them, on the reading that the 0.36 s blip at 7.28 is the "...and" the Warden's line opens with - the ellipsis in the subtitle is the only evidence for that and it is an inference. If the Lord's line actually runs on to 7.64, move the 6.9 to about 8.0 and the 6.6 down to match. THIS IS THE MISTAKE captions.json warns about: energy says where sound is, never which words are inside it.

THE THANK-YOU CARD reuses dragon_lord_defeated_2's picture rather than carrying art of its own, by the author's call - there was no third panel drawn and a second look at the Warden on his cliff is a better last frame than a black one. It is the only card in the game that can be skipped, because it is the last thing between a finished game and the flag.

IT IS SET, NOT SUBTITLED, and it is the only card in the game that is. `end_card: true` switches the layout - see _set_end_card in game/session.gd - so instead of a `caption` in the band at the foot it gets a centred stack: `end_title` over a rule, `caption` under it, `end_credit` at the foot. It had been a caption, which meant the last thing the game said arrived in the same typography the Dragon Lord had been shouting in, on a third look at his panel, and then faded out; it read as one more line of dialogue rather than as an ending.

`end_title` is the GAME's name and not this level's. The level is called The Dragon's Roost and what is being thanked for is the whole thing, so the card names it and the level-title fallback in _set_end_card does not run here.

TWO DIFFERENT DIMS meet on this card and they are not the same thing. STORY_DIM takes the LEVEL down behind every card, so the panel reads as the screen; END_SCRIM takes the PANEL down so set text can be read over it. The scrim has to sit ABOVE the art in the story layer - story_dim sits below it - and putting it in the wrong place is how the first attempt at this came up as a full-brightness close-up of the Warden's face with the title lost in his hair. Both ride the card's own dissolve, so nothing flashes bright on the way in or out.

`hold` is 6.5 rather than the 5.0 it was as a caption: there are three lines to read now instead of one, and this is the last card before the fade. It carries no audio of its own - dragon_lord_defeated has finished by the time it is up - and `keep_audio` is what stops it restarting the clip, which also means it arrives through _begin_swap rather than _begin_story. tests/capture_endcard.gd shoots it.
